DIRECTIONS 100 W 84th St, New York, NY 10024 Nearest Trains: 1 train to 79 th or 86 th Street, B or C trains at 81 st or 86 th Street SECTIONS • Unrated – unrated players U200 (4 rounds, no clock) • Novice – U600 (4 rounds, G/25 d5) • Reserve – USCF Under 1000 (4 rounds, G/25 d5) • Advanced – USCF Under 1400 (4 rounds, G/25 d5) Tie-breaks: Modified Median, Solkoff. events.description: Tournament Start Times: Championship: Mandatory Check in 8:30 – 9:00. Pairings out at 9:15 AM Future Masters and Classic: Pairings at 9:15 AM Reserve: 9:30 AM Booster: Pairings at 9:45 AM K-4 U600, K-1 U400, Novice: 10:00 AM start time Novice Novice is a section for those who are brand new to Chess Novice 1: Open to PK-1st Grade students who are Unrated. Students play 4 Rounds. If total round time exceeds 40 minutes, clocks will be provided with 5 minutes per player. Tiebreakers will be used if necessary. Trophies for Top 10 placements, participation trophies for all other players. Novice 2: Open to 2-4th Grade students who are Unrated. Students play 4 Rounds. If total round time exceeds 40 minutes, clocks will be provided with 5 minutes per player. Tiebreakers will be used if necessary. Trophies for Top 10 placements K-1 U400, K-4 U600, K-8 U800, K-12 U1100, Classic 1000-1299, Future Masters 1200-1500, Championship: 1500+ Players must have a valid USCF ID Trophies will go to the top 10 players in each section and medals for all other participants. Team trophy given to top performing team Championship: 1500+: This is a new section created to draw the most competitive tournament at Avenues. There will be 4 rounds at g 50 d/5. This section is open to only those rated above 1500. Free entry for players 1800+. $350 in cash prizes, based on 12 entries: $200 to first, $100 to 2nd and $50 to 3rd Future Masters 1200-1500: There will be 4 rounds at g/50 d5. Top 5 receive trophies Classic 1000-1299: This section is for players rated 1000-1299. The time control will be g/40 d5. 4 rounds K-12 Reserve U1100: G40/d5, 4 Rounds. Tiebreakers will be used if necessary. Trophies for Top 10, Medals for all other participants. Open to current USCF members in grades K-12 who are <1100 USCF rated using the higher of USCF Online Regular rating and USCF Regular over the board ratings. K-8 Booster U800: This is a section for players in K-8 who are rated <800. There will be 4 rounds at G/30 d5. Trophies to top 10 players and medals for all others. Team trophy to top performing school team K-4 Primary U600: This is a section for players in K-4 rated <600. There will be 4 games at g/30 d5. Top 10 receive trophies and the rest receive medals. There is also a top team trophy given to the top team in the section K-1 U400: This is a section for players in K-1 rated U400. Place trophies for the top 10 players, participation trophies to all others. 4 rounds g/30 d5 Schedule Check in is from 8:30 – 9:00 AM for Championship. All other players please arrive 20-30 minutes before your section is set to start. Rounds will begin as soon as all games in the section have concluded. There will be a short grace period before the next match pairings are posted. Entry Fee and Other Information Early bird entry fee: $59 by Monday 11:00 PM before tournament, regular entry fee: $69 We are using the monthly supplement rating for section determination. The only exception is for the Championship section, which can be determined by live ratings Registration deadline is Friday before tournament at 5:00 PM – We are not accepting on site registrations Refund policy: No refunds within 24 hours of the tournament. If you request a refund, you can be issued a full credit towards a future tournament. Alternatively, you can get a full refund less a $10 service charge. Time controls: Championship: 4 rounds at g 50 d/5 Future Masters: 4 rounds g 50 d/5 Classic: 4 rounds at g 40 d/5 Reserve: 4 rounds at g 40 d/5 K-1 U400, K-4 U600, Booster K-8 U800: 4 rounds at g 30 d/5 Novice1 and 2: No clocks

events.description: PS41 Chess Tournament 116 West 11th Street Manhattan 2025-26 Tournament dates: October 13, November 9, March 1, and May 17 Open to first 156 players – Register using the link at the bottom of the page $50 per player (proceeds supporting the PS41 Chess Team) UNRATED SECTIONS Board and pieces will be supplied, and no clocks will be used. U.S. Chess Federation membership is not required for these sections. Please arrive 15 minutes before your start time. Special instructions for our Unrated Sections will be presented at 10:15am in the auditorium. No Score (Kindergarten Only) 4 rounds. Start / Est. End Time: 10:30am / 2:30pm. This section is specially designed for K children new to chess tournaments and might not remember all the rules. Tournament Directors will guide the children and results will not be recorded. Trophies awarded to all players. K-1 Novice (Kindergartners and First Grade) 4 rounds. Start / Est. End Time: 10:30am / 2:30pm. Trophies awarded to winners. Medals for all other players. 2-5 Novice (2nd to 5th Grade) 4 rounds. Start / Est. End Time: 10:30am / 2:30pm. Trophies awarded to winners. Medals for all other players. USCF RATED SECTIONS Players in these sections must play with a clock. Board and pieces will be supplied but bring clocks if you have them. U.S. Chess Federation membership is required for rated sections. Please arrive 15 minutes before your start time. Juniors (K-1st Grade, USCF Under 600) 4 rounds, G/40 d5. Start / Est. End Time: 10am / 3:30pm . Trophies to winners. Medals for all other players. Primary (K-3rd Grade, USCF Under 800) 4 rounds, G/40 d5. Start / Est. End Time: 10am / 3:30pm . Trophies to winners. Medals for all other players. Reserve (K-8th Grade, USCF Under 1100) 4 rounds, G/40 d5. Start / Est. End Time: 9:45am / 4pm . Trophies to winners. Medals for all other players. Championship (K-12th Grade, USCF 1000-1400) 4 rounds, G/45 d5. Start / Est. End Time: 9:30am / 4pm . Trophies to winners. Medals for all other players. Tournament Details * Special instructions for our Unrated Sections will be presented at 10:15am in the auditorium. * Pairing will be posted in the Playing Hall (cafeteria) * Parents may help their children get settled in the playing hall at the start of their rounds. * Parents should wait in the auditorium while games are played – Spectating games is not allowed. * Second and following rounds will begin when the previous round is completed. * Award ceremonies will take place at the completion of each section. Lunch – Pizza Pizza slices will be on sale or participants can bring their own food and should bring their own water bottle. Important Information PARENTAL SUPERVISION IS REQUIRED THROUGHOUT THE TOURNAMENT NO FOOD OR DRINKS ARE ALLOWED IN THE AUDITORIUM

events.summary: 2025-2026: Oct 5, Dec 7, Nov 9, Jan 25, Feb 22, Mar 15, Apr 19 **LOCATION CHANGE** – 4 West 93rd Street – Library We are open to players in Grades 7-12 (who are also born after 4/21/2005). Players can play as individuals as well as part of a school team. We have both individual...
events.description: 2025-2026: Oct 5, Dec 7, Nov 9, Jan 25, Feb 22, Mar 15, Apr 19 **LOCATION CHANGE** – 4 West 93rd Street – Library We are open to players in Grades 7-12 (who are also born after 4/21/2005). Players can play as individuals as well as part of a school team. We have both individual and team prizes! We also have Mixed Doubles Teams Bonus Prizes ! Mixed Doubles teams are two players, one male, one female (they can be from any sections and any schools), with an average team rating Under 2200 at signup deadline. Players must sign up by January 28th for Mixed Doubles. We have four separate sections. 1 . Varsity, for players rated 1800 and above (at match date or within the prior 12 months, and invitees); 2. Junior-Varsity, for players whose Official Rating is Under 2000 at match date or Unrateds; 3. Novice, for players whose Official Rating is Under 1400 at match date or Unrateds; 4. Under 900, for players whose Official Rating is Under 900 at match date or Unrateds. We have two rounds each date– at about 10:00 am (all sections) and then about 12:30 pm (Under 900); about 1:30 pm (Varsity, Junior-Varsity and Novice)– earlier if feasible. Our Magnus League time controls: Varsity, Junior-Varsity and Novice: Game/60 + 30-second delay; Novice: Game/60 + 10-second delay (please bring a delay clock if you have one). Presented By The Chess Center of New York and Little House Of Chess With Grateful Appreciation to Columbia Grammar and Preparatory School For more details, please visit Magnusleague.org Tournament Information and Online Registration are coming soon. Contact info: director@magnusleague.org

events.description: **Location Change for March & April Tournaments** Reserve, Classic & Premier will be played at 4 West 93rd Library for March & April tournaments. K, 1, and 2-3 U700 will continue to take place at 26 W 94th. Open to Students in Grades K-12 in 6 sections. US Chess Federation rated for all sections. Online registration will close 11 pm the day before the tournament . No entries on site! Early bird registration fee is $50 for CGPS students, $60 for everyone else. ($15 added to all registrations after Tuesday night– within 72 hours of tournament. We have a $20 refund fee.) Discount $5 per paying sibling. Free entry if you are rated over 1500! Current US Chess membership required: $20 (age 19 and under) Friday 4 pm at The Columbia Grammar School Gym/Cafeteria at 26 West 94th Sections Rating Rounds Time Notation Byes Kindergarten All 4 No clock used Optional 0 or 1 1st Grade All 4 No clock used Optional 0 or 1 2nd/3rd Grade Under 700 4 No clock used Optional 0 or 1 Limited to first 50 players. Sets and boards provided. Friday 4 pm at the Library of 4 West 93rd Sections Rating Rounds Time Notation Byes Reserve (K-12) Under 900 3 Game 50 +5 sec delay Yes 0 or 1 Classic (K-12) 800 to 1199 3 Game 50 + 5 sec delay Yes 0 or 1 Premier (K-12) 1200 and up 3 Game 50 + 5 sec delay Yes No Limited to first 50 players. Sets and boards provided. Top 3 sections: Please bring clocks! Live ratings may be used at TD discretion; TD reserves right to assign players’ sections and to combine sections. Players winning their section usually moves up in the next tournament. Electronic score sheets not allowed! Schedule: The first round begins at 4pm. K through 3rd grade sections end around 7:45 pm. Other sections finish around 8:30 pm. The next round will begin as soon as possible after the previous round ends. Awards: Premier Quads prize: Free entry (value $50) into Marshall or G & T Quads. Other sections: Trophies to top 15 in each section. Honored Participant trophies to everyone else. Award ceremonies as soon as possible after each section concludes. Important: We are a nut free tournament! Please do not bring nuts or nut-containing items. Do not attend if experiencing symptoms. Please maintain good “health etiquette” — wash your hands frequently, cover sneezes and coughs, etc. Parent or designate must be present to assert parental supervision over your child’s behavior and activities. Little House of Chess, Inc does not provide supervision when a child has finished a scheduled game. Email: littlehouseofchess@gmail.com if you have questions.
